observations.statement: Planning Wizard is defined as the planning workspace that accepts three prose-level input forms and produces implementation-ready Plans, a Final Plan Pack, and an ApprovedPlanPack gated by explicit Approve And Build approval.

The window assigns Planning Wizard ownership of planning aggregates, topic work, audits, integration, amendments, readiness, GUI states, ApprovedPlanPack authority, and approval transition while explicitly excluding low-level execution after Executor activation.

Planning Wizard may initiate multiple web and browser operations when external evidence materially changes planning, but their receipts, citations, artifacts, closure, and failures remain planning evidence rather than runtime or compile authority.
PWIZ-001 fixes the canonical product name, enumerates exactly three canonical seed families, requires provenance and contextual fields, and replaces raw-transcript copying with a structured handoff.

The plan compile hint and acceptance boundary explicitly prohibit creating WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, runtime artifacts, implementation files, governance artifacts, or production build tasks in this planning compile.
The production final-review control has a fixed command token and a payload inventory spanning project/run identity, revisions, hashes, approval actor, and deterministic idempotency key.
Approval is specified to fail closed on stale reviewed inputs and route to bounded revalidation or final-review refresh without silently substituting a different plan.

Successful approval is specified as an atomic receipt/event/run operation that synchronously returns durable run identity and deduplicates identical CAS/idempotency deliveries to the same PlanCompileRun.

Execution-unit context and persisted approval events are delegated to named SSOT contracts; local field copies are forbidden, schema_version is required for embedded context, and secret-bearing values are prohibited.
Approve And Build is the sole ordinary GUI approval-to-PlanCompileRun launch authority, with four alternative ordinary build-launch labels explicitly prohibited.
PlanningRun is a parent aggregate over bounded child threads and a broad field inventory; project context is modeled independently from work intent and compatible delivery intents may overlap.
Topic structure is evidence-driven rather than universally fixed, supports a broad mutation set, and exposes suggested navigation while allowing reopening and parallel background work.

Every substantive exchange must append an event and update affected planning state before turn completion; each topic uses a bounded capsule and fresh bounded agent, with gap-driven questions, safe defaults, and a restricted HITL boundary.

The context-only continuation says topic records share one Planning Run ledger, names dependency-staleness states, classifies new information, and keeps Approved PRD Packs immutable; this context is not used to substantiate a core finding.

candidate_findings.title: Canonical seed families lack bound data contracts
candidate_findings.statement: The core names exactly three canonical seed families and lists information they preserve, but it does not bind any family to a schema identifier or define field types, requiredness, normalization, size bounds, version compatibility, hash validation, warning validation, or reject/error behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Independent producers can emit structurally different seeds under the same family token, making intake validation, provenance preservation, and deterministic replay builder-dependent.

candidate_findings.title: Assistant Chat fast path blurs the exact three-family gate
candidate_findings.statement: The same canonical text that permits exactly three seed families also says Assistant Chat may construct a traceable seed or draft PRD Pack and begin intake, without stating which canonical family a draft PRD Pack becomes or what approval/readiness transition makes it admissible.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can treat a draft pack as an implicit fourth input or bypass ApprovedPRDPack readiness differently, producing inconsistent intake and approval behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Research self-initiation lacks an operational authority contract
candidate_findings.statement: The trigger when external information materially changes planning and the list of allowed web/browser operations do not define who authorizes external access, budget or depth limits, source trust/freshness thresholds, repository or credential boundaries, cancellation, timeout, retry, deduplication, concurrency, or the condition for research closure versus failure.
candidate_findings.impact: Research behavior can become unbounded, non-repeatable, privacy-sensitive, or inconsistent across implementations, and planning may advance on different evidence sets.

candidate_findings.title: Approval actor is carried but authorization is not specified
candidate_findings.statement: The approval command carries an approval actor and Planning Wizard consumes permissions and HITL contracts, yet the core defines no eligible actor roles, permission check, authentication binding, separation-of-duties rule, or authorization-failure result for Approve And Build.
candidate_findings.impact: A builder must invent who can authorize Plan Compile, risking unauthorized launches or incompatible permission enforcement across GUI and command consumers.

candidate_findings.title: Approval failure and atomic recovery protocol is incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: The core specifies stale-input failure and a successful atomic multi-effect transition, but not malformed payload, missing-currentness, unauthorized, persistence, publish, PlanCompileRun creation, timeout, cancellation, or transaction-conflict outcomes; it also leaves commit ordering, rollback, retry after indeterminate completion, and recovery from partial cross-component failure undefined.
candidate_findings.impact: Failures can produce orphan receipts, duplicate or missing events, multiple runs, or an approval whose caller cannot determine whether retry is safe.

candidate_findings.title: PlanningRun lifecycle is an inventory rather than a state model
candidate_findings.statement: PlanningRun owns status, hashes, events, invalidations, audits, amendments, drafts, and final pack state, but the core gives no allowed status values, transition graph, transition authorities, revision/CAS rules, terminal states, cancellation, pause/resume, reopen, retry, retention, or serialization contract.
candidate_findings.impact: Lifecycle gates and currentness checks can diverge, and the approval CAS cannot be implemented consistently against an undefined aggregate transition model.

candidate_findings.title: Topic mutations and parallel work lack deterministic conflict semantics
candidate_findings.statement: The controller may add, split, merge, rename, defer, reopen, reorder, and impact topics while the GUI allows parallel background work, but the core does not define operation inputs/outputs, stable identity and lineage, dependency-cycle handling, preconditions, ordering, concurrent edit detection, merge resolution, invalidation propagation, or idempotency.
candidate_findings.impact: Equivalent user actions can yield different topic graphs, lost updates, cyclic dependencies, or drafts that remain apparently current after conflicting parallel mutations.

candidate_findings.title: Topic event and state durability lacks atomicity and envelope rules
candidate_findings.statement: Every substantive exchange must append an event and update several state classes before turn completion, but the requirement does not define a transaction boundary, causal ordering, event identity, idempotent retry, partial-write rollback, or recovery; the EventRecord delegation in this window is expressly scoped to approval, PlanApproved, and final-review events rather than topic exchanges.
candidate_findings.impact: A crash or duplicate delivery can leave an event without matching state, state without an event, or repeated planning atoms, breaking replay, audit lineage, and the prohibition on advancing unsynchronized chat state.

candidate_findings.title: Bounded agent and capsule semantics are qualitative
candidate_findings.statement: The core calls threads, agents, capsules, and relevant-source sets bounded, but supplies no token, byte, turn, time, source-count, or cost limits; it also omits capsule schema/version/hash, freshness, refresh, truncation, priority, redaction, and overflow behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can silently omit different context, leak overbroad history, or exhaust resources while still claiming conformance to a bounded capsule.

candidate_findings.title: Safe-default and HITL classification authority is not testable
candidate_findings.statement: The controller may decide that a gap is auto-resolvable, apply a safe default, defer a detail, or decide that user direction is genuinely required, but no evidence precedence, confidence threshold, conflict rule, risk taxonomy, destructive-authority test, assumption expiry, escalation state, or resume behavior is specified.
candidate_findings.impact: Material product decisions may be silently defaulted or needlessly blocked based on builder judgment, with no deterministic oracle for correct escalation.

candidate_findings.title: Behavioral acceptance evidence is not mapped to the normative contracts
candidate_findings.statement: PWIZ-001 and PWIZ-004 list plan-index and ledger validation commands, but the window does not state fixtures, assertions, receipts, or expected results that connect those surfaces to seed validation, stale CAS rejection, authorization, atomic approval, duplicate delivery, GUI command exclusivity, topic synchronization, or safe-default behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: A green listed validator result cannot by itself demonstrate that the consequential runtime and GUI contracts in this window are satisfied.

candidate_findings.title: GUI state and accessibility behavior is underspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The GUI can suggest navigation, route stale approval to refresh or revalidation, and expose the sole launch control, but the core does not define visible states, disabled-state conditions for that final control, progress and error presentation, focus/keyboard behavior, screen-reader names, announcements, recovery affordances, or stale-projection reconciliation in the Planning Wizard surface.
candidate_findings.impact: Users can receive inconsistent or inaccessible approval and topic-navigation experiences, including unclear reasons why approval cannot proceed or whether a retry is safe.

candidate_findings.title: Dependency metadata does not encode stated contract reliance
candidate_findings.statement: The ownership prose names many consumed systems and contracts, while PWIZ-001 and PWIZ-003 declare empty depends_on and unblocks arrays; the window does not explain whether these external prerequisites are intentionally outside PlanUnit dependency semantics or where their readiness is represented.
candidate_findings.impact: Plan graph, readiness, and compile ordering consumers may treat contract-dependent behavior as dependency-free or make incompatible assumptions about prerequisite availability.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Canonical naming is explicit: Planning Wizard is current and Chain Wizard and Plan Wizard are stale names to retire from active prose, UI, commands, events, and contracts.
The input-family count and tokens are explicit, and seed provenance, warnings, lineage, context, and compatible work-intent preservation are normative.
The Assistant Chat handoff must be structured and the raw transcript cannot be the sole handoff.
Research receipts and artifacts are explicitly planning evidence only and cannot independently create execution or Plan Compile authority.
This planning/addendum scope explicitly excludes WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, implementation/runtime artifacts, production tasks, generated governance artifacts, and governance sealing.
The stale-review safety invariant is explicit and fail-closed; a changed plan cannot be silently approved under the prior review.
Successful approval explicitly produces one durable PlanCompileRun identity synchronously and duplicate identical delivery returns that same run.
Execution context and event envelope ownership are explicitly delegated to named canonical contracts, and local field copying plus secret persistence are prohibited.
Ordinary GUI launch authority and prohibited alternative labels are explicit, including the distinction between final planning approval and later scoped runtime controls.
Project context is explicitly independent from work intent, and the model permits more than one compatible delivery intent.
The topic taxonomy is explicitly evidence-driven, a fixed universal taxonomy is prohibited, and the supported mutation verbs are enumerated.
Fresh topic-agent isolation, topic relevance, durable synchronization before advance, non-generic questions, and the rule against turning ordinary uncertainty into a user blocker are explicit.
Context-only text explicitly keeps Approved PRD Packs immutable and routes later information into amendments, out-of-scope items, or revision requests instead of in-place source mutation.

unknowns.statement: The exact schemas, field types, cardinalities, validation rules, and compatibility rules for ApprovedPRDPack, normalized_requirements_pack, assistant_chat_handoff_seed, Final Plan Pack, and ApprovedPlanPack are not present in the assigned window.
The precise permission and HITL contracts that determine who may approve and how an approval actor is authenticated are outside the assigned evidence.
The exact execution_unit_context and EventRecord field sets are unknown here because the window delegates them to named external contracts that blind scope forbids reading.

Dispatcher request/receipt schemas, browser evidence retention, source-selection policy, research closure criteria, and operation-level retry/cancellation semantics are not defined in the assigned window.
PlanningRun status values, transitions, cancellation and retry states, persistence representation, and revision generation remain unknown within this core.
Topic-operation command names and payloads, graph invariants, dependency edge types, cycle policy, concurrency control, and merge/split identity rules remain unknown.
The event schema and transaction/replay rules for ordinary substantive topic exchanges remain unknown; the explicit EventRecord sentence only names approval-related persisted events.
The measurable meanings of substantive, bounded, auto-resolvable, safe default, downstream-only, genuine product direction, and irreconcilable ambiguity are not supplied.
The behavioral coverage and expected pass/fail output of the two named validation commands cannot be determined without leaving the blind window.
Accessibility requirements and exact GUI projections for topic navigation, stale approval, disabled controls, progress, and recovery are not present in this assigned core.
The context continuation gives partial invalidation and amendment vocabulary, but any additional PWIZ-005 contract beyond canonical lines 353-364 is outside scope and was not used to close core gaps.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_quote: Planning Wizard is the finished-product planning workspace that consumes an Approved PRD Pack, normalized requirements input, or structured Assistant Chat seed and turns it into implementation-ready Plans, a Final Plan Pack, and an ApprovedPlanPack suitable for Plan Compile after explicit `Approve And Build` approval.

Planning Wizard owns PlanningRun, topic graph, topic agents, topic-scoped ledger work, Planning Context Capsules, topic conversion and audits, final integration, Planning Amendments, compile readiness, ApprovedPlanPack authority, Planning Wizard GUI states, and the Approve And Build transition. It consumes PRD Builder, Assistant Chat, Goal Runtime, Plan Document System, Plan To Node Compilation, Automated Testing, Executor, Contracts, source-control, permissions, Final GUI, Orchestrator, and HITL contracts without owning low-level runtime execution after Executor activation.

Planning Wizard may self-initiate web/search/fetch/extract/research/deep-research/crawl/map (`websearch`, `webfetch`, `webextract`, `webresearch`, `webcrawl`, `webmap`) and Site Reader/browser evidence through the shared PM WebOperation/BrowserAction dispatcher when current external facts, docs, issues, PRs, URLs, visual/dynamic pages, project context, comparative research, or source authority materially changes planning.

The resulting read receipts, extract receipts, citations, browser artifacts, source-selection reasons, research closure states, and failure states are planning evidence only until explicit approval; they may flow into Planning Context Capsules, topic ledgers, topic plans, audit findings, Final Plan Pack source refs, and ApprovedPlanPack lineage, but they do not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, runtime code, implementation files, production build tasks, or Plan Compile authority by themselves.
The canonical product name is Planning Wizard; Chain Wizard and Plan Wizard are stale names that must be retired from active product prose, UI, commands, events, and contracts.
Planning Wizard accepts exactly three canonical input seed families before topic work begins: ApprovedPRDPack, normalized_requirements_pack, or assistant_chat_handoff_seed.

Each seed preserves source identity, version, hashes, warnings, amendments, lineage, project context, and bounded work_intent axes; multiple compatible intents such as feature work plus release PR delivery may overlap in one PlanningRun without collapsing project context into a single lossy mode enum.

Send to Planning Wizard creates a structured seed containing goal, scope, project, requirements, assumptions, open questions, source message references, artifacts, repository context, and suggested mode rather than copying an unbounded transcript.

When Assistant Chat already contains sufficient planning-intake intent, the handoff may construct a traceable seed or draft PRD Pack and begin Planning Wizard intake without forcing the user through repeated PRD Builder questions.
- Canonical input seeds preserve identity, version/hash, warnings, lineage, project context, and multiple compatible work_intent axes.

  create_nodeseeds: false
- Do not use the raw Assistant Chat transcript as the sole Planning Wizard handoff.

This addendum closes the Approve And Build defects from the PMConcept readiness report. It does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, implementation files, runtime dispatch, generated governance artifacts, or a governance seal.

The production final-review control dispatches `cmd.planning_wizard.approve_and_build`. The command payload carries the exact final-review CAS/currentness values shown to the user: `project_id`, `planning_run_id`, PlanningRun revision, topic map version, `approved_plan_pack_id`, pack version/hash, project-context snapshot hash, PlanUnit index hash, acceptance-unit index hash, testing policy hash, final audit/closure hash, approval actor, and deterministic idempotency key.

Approval fails closed when any planning state, source pack, project context, topic readiness, audit closure, testing policy, Plan index input, or displayed final-review CAS input changed after the user reviewed it. A stale failure routes to bounded revalidation or final-review refresh; it must not silently approve a different plan.

Successful approval atomically writes `approval_cas_receipt`, publishes `PlanApproved`, creates or binds exactly one `PlanCompileRun`, and returns the durable `plan_compile_run_id` synchronously. Projection reconciliation may show a pending launch shell in Orchestrator Plan Compile, but run identity itself may not be left to eventual projection. Duplicate delivery with the same CAS inputs and idempotency key returns the same `PlanCompileRun`.

Planning Wizard and PlanApproved records consume `execution_unit_context` only through the Executor-owned contract in `Plans/Executor_Protocol.md` and `Plans/execution_unit_context.schema.json`. They must not define a local context field list, must not persist an embedded context payload without `schema_version`, and must not store secrets, tokens, passwords, credentials, API keys, provider auth values, or local machine secrets in the context payload.

Persisted Planning Wizard approval, PlanApproved, and final-review events consume the canonical EventRecord envelope in `Plans/Contracts_V0.md#EventRecord` and `Plans/event_record.schema.json`. Planning Wizard owns approval behavior and CAS/idempotency semantics, but it must not copy the EventRecord field set or treat the EventRecord schema as permission to emit PlanCompile runtime artifacts.

The Planning Wizard and PMConcept concept surface must not expose `START`, `BUILD`, `Start Chain`, or `Approve & Continue` as ordinary build-launch controls. `Approve And Build` is the only ordinary final planning approval-to-PlanCompileRun launch authority; later controls are post-approval Plan Compile or runtime controls with scoped commands, disabled reasons, receipt effects, and stale-projection behavior.

Each planning topic, integration pass, and attached audit/repair activity is a bounded child thread grouped by planning_run_id and thread_group_id under one collapsible Planning Run parent. PlanningRun owns source pack identity, project and work-intent context, thread group, global planning ledger, dynamic topic map, topic threads, topic plan drafts, amendments, invalidations, audit cycles, final plan pack, status, hashes, and handoff events.

Planning Wizard classifies project context independently from work intent so overlapping cases such as an existing Git repository plus feature work plus PR delivery are represented without a misleading single mode enum. Project context supports greenfield, existing local project, existing Git repository, remote SSH project, and fork or external upstream contexts, with explicit repository and host facts. Work intent supports new product, feature or enhancement, refactor or rewrite,
  bugfix or bounded task, and contribution PR, and may include more than one compatible delivery intent.
- Do not use one unbounded transcript for the entire Planning Wizard.

Planning Wizard derives an initial topic graph from the input pack, project/repository context, work intent, risk, and known defaults rather than enforcing a fixed list of sections. Possible topics include overview, product behavior, GUI or UX, backend, data, integrations, security, permissions, testing, deployment, migration, observability, and risks, but actual titles and scope are evidence-driven.
The controller can add, split, merge, rename, defer, reopen, reorder, and mark topics impacted, recording the reason, source refs, dependencies, user-visible origin, and resulting invalidations.
The GUI suggests a next topic and conversational sequence while the underlying topic map preserves dependencies and allows safe navigation, reopening, and parallel background work.

- Do not hardcode one universal topic taxonomy for all projects.

Every substantive Planning Wizard exchange must append an event and update topic-scoped planning atoms plus any affected global decisions, constraints, dependencies, invalidations, amendments, questions, and handoff state before the turn is complete.

Each topic agent receives a bounded Planning Context Capsule containing approved PRD summary, project context, global decisions and constraints, glossary, relevant prior topic-plan summaries, dependencies, assumptions, questions, and artifact references.
Each topic conversation is handled by a fresh topic agent with a bounded thread, topic brief, Context Capsule, relevant sources, and topic-scoped write card.
Each topic agent asks gap-driven questions relevant to its active topic and implementation-readiness risks, using known answers and defaults so it does not drift into unrelated domains.

Planning Wizard proactively resolves behavior, state, data, identity, permissions,
  failure modes, edge cases, integration constraints, acceptance evidence, currentness, idempotency, migration, operations, and implementation boundaries.

The controller answers auto-resolvable gaps from evidence, applies safe defaults with recorded assumptions, and defers downstream-only details; it asks the user only for genuine product direction, risk acceptance, destructive authority, credentials, legal policy, or irreconcilable ambiguity.

A later decision that changes a prior topic''s assumptions or outputs marks affected topic drafts stale_due_to_dependency_change, stale_due_to_new_scope, or requires_recompile/requires_reaudit and propagates impact through typed topic dependencies.

New information during planning becomes a planning clarification, immutable Planning Amendment, out_of_current_approved_scope item, or PRD revision request according to materiality and impact. Approved PRD Packs remain immutable; Planning Wizard records amendments or requests a successor PRD rather than editing the approved source snapshot in place.
